payload.findings_fixed:
One finding, and it was a REAL DEFECT IN THIS ITERATION'S OWN CODE rather than a stale test - the battery earned its keep.

FINDING: tests/i5b-e2e.test.ts failed at "the worktree branch merged to trunk". The temptation was to read it as a test encoding the old, defective contract - the new close refuses an empty branch, which is the whole point of R2 - and to update the test. That reading was wrong. The e2e walks a real iteration and ships it, so its branch SHOULD have carried milestone commits, and it did not.

ROOT CAUSE in c4's wiring: bless() decided whether an iteration was worktree-resident by asking whether the instance file existed under its OWN root. That is true in two different situations - a genuinely trunk-resident iteration, AND a Gate constructed with the worktree root itself, which is exactly what the e2e does. In the second case the bless concluded 'trunk-resident', skipped the milestone commit, and left an empty branch that the new close then correctly refused. Every one of my own milestone checks missed it because they call commitMilestone directly with the trunk root; only the end-to-end walk exercised the worktree-rooted caller.

FIX: a new projectRootOf() in worktree.ts resolves the PROJECT root for a root that may itself be a worktree (a caller inside .worktrees/<id> is working on the project two levels up), and bless() now resolves the stream from that project root and commits the milestone there. Both callers - trunk-rooted server and worktree-rooted Gate - now recognise the same stream. The structural guard was updated to pin the corrected resolution rather than the old argument, and it gained an assertion that the stream is resolved from the project root, so this specific confusion cannot return silently.

Evidence: i5b-e2e 1/1, rails 8/8, i5b-worktrees-live 3/3, imports-readonly 4/4 (run-c9957aadb38f), with the iteration's own suite re-run after the guard update.
